cases.sentence: Для истории признание свободы людей как силы, могущей влиять на ___, т. е. не подчиненной законам, есть то же, чтó для астрономии признание свободной силы движения небесных сил.
cases.explain: «исторические события» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The recognition of man’s free will as something capable of influencing historical events, that is, as not subject to laws, is the same for history as the recognition of a free force moving the heavenly bodies would be for astronomy.

cases.sentence: Если существует хоть одно свободно двигающееся тело, то не существует более законов Келлера и Ньютона и не существует более никакого представления о движении ___.
cases.explain: «небесных тел» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: That assumption would destroy the possibility of the existence of laws, that is, of any science whatever. If there is even a single body moving freely, then the laws of Kepler and Newton are negatived and no conception of the movement of the heavenly bodies any longer exists. If any single action is due to free will, then not a single historical law can exist, nor any conception of historical events.

cases.sentence: Придя к бесконечно-малому, математика, точнейшая из наук, оставляет процесс дробления и приступает к ___ суммования неизвестных бесконечно-малых.
cases.explain: «новому процессу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: All human sciences have traveled along that path. Arriving at infinitesimals, mathematics, the most exact of sciences, abandons the process of analysis and enters on the new process of the integration of unknown, infinitely small, quantities. Abandoning the conception of cause, mathematics seeks law, that is, the property common to all unknown, infinitely small, elements.

cases.sentence: Хотя и в ___, но по тому же пути мышления шли и другие науки.
cases.explain: «другой форме» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: In another form but along the same path of reflection the other sciences have proceeded. When Newton enunciated the law of gravity he did not say that the sun or the earth had a property of attraction; he said that all bodies from the largest to the smallest have the property of attracting one another, that is, leaving aside the question of the cause of the movement of the bodies, he expressed the property common to all bodies from the infinitely large to the infinitely small. The same is done by the natural sciences: leaving aside the question of cause, they seek for laws. History stands on the same path. And if history has for its object the study of the movement of the nations and of humanity and not the narration of episodes in the lives of individuals, it too, setting aside the conception of cause, should seek the laws common to all the inseparably interconnected infinitesimal elements of free will.
